document_title: 2025 Clinical Practice Guidelines for Multimodal Cardiovascular Risk Assessment
source: American Heart Association / ACC Clinical Guidelines (2025)

sections.section_name: Section 1.1: Fasting Blood Glucose and Metabolic Anomalies
sections.content: Fasting blood glucose levels exceeding 126 mg/dL indicate metabolic dysfunction and significantly elevate long-term cardiovascular disease risk. When combined with elevated systolic blood pressure (>140 mmHg), microvascular and macrovascular injury risk increases quadratically. Clinicians must evaluate glucose dysregulation alongside cardiac troponin-T markers.

sections.section_name: Section 2.3: Cardiac Troponin-T and Acute Myocardial Stress
sections.content: Serum Troponin-T levels greater than 0.04 ng/mL serve as a definitive biomarker for myocardial injury and ischemic stress. In patients presenting with high model risk scores (>0.75), troponin elevation mandates immediate electrocardiographic monitoring and cardiology triage.

sections.section_name: Section 3.4: Systolic and Diastolic Blood Pressure Management
sections.content: Systolic blood pressure exceeding 130 mmHg or diastolic pressure exceeding 80 mmHg defines Stage 1 hypertension. Persistent arterial pressure combined with elevated LDL cholesterol (>130 mg/dL) accelerates atherogenesis and coronary artery stenosis.

document_title: Diagnostic Imaging Standards for Multimodal Cardiac and Thoracic Pathology
source: Journal of Thoracic and Volumetric Imaging (2024)

sections.content: Chest X-Ray radiographs evaluated via dense neural feature extraction (TorchXRayVision DenseNet-121 / MerMED ViT) detect cardiomegaly, pulmonary vascular congestion, and pleural effusions. Radiographic abnormalities combined with high-risk clinical biomarkers confirm advanced cardiopulmonary distress.

sections.section_name: Section 5.2: 3D Volumetric CT and MRI Scans
sections.content: 3D volumetric scans processed via 3D ResNet-10 (MedicalNet) extract volumetric spatial representations of ventricular geometry and ischemic lesions. Spatial feature integration provides high sensitivity for structural cardiac anomalies.
